name: Bambassi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Ahland 2012 A Grammar of Northern Mao (776pp, U Oregon) READ in full text: tone-only prosody, no word-stress statement; no other stress source found.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page bamb1262 (dialects Kere kere1282, Nuclear Bambassi nucl1341); Scholars' Bank DSpace records for items 1794/12456 (dissertation) and 1794/19944 (supplement = audio files only)
sources.note: Records only; used to locate files and confirm no further descriptive titles beyond the six in the target record.

sources.citation: Ahland, Michael Bryan. 2012. A grammar of Northern Mao (Màwés Aas'è). PhD dissertation, University of Oregon, xxxiv+742 pp. (PDF 775 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. II 'Contrastive phonology' (pp. 52-94, incl. 2.4 syllable structure, 2.5 tonal melodies) and Ch. III 'Tone' (pp. 95-192) describe a three-level tone system (H, M, L; M with two underlying sources; downstep; construct-noun melodies; tone as stem-category marker). a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence/intensity returns only non-phonological uses ('distress', 'stress that', a remark about Amharic pronoun stress p. ~400, and 'increase in volume and a higher register' for pragmatic emphasis on a demonstrative, ch. 6). No word-stress or accent statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Ahland, Michael (2009). Aspects of Northern Mao Phonology. Linguistic Discovery 7. pp. 1-40.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Language is not in the catalog and has no existing statements; the work gives tone facts only and is silent on word stress, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict.

sources.citation: Ahland, Michael. 2009. Aspects of Northern Mao (Bambassi-Diddesa) phonology. Linguistic Discovery 7(1): 1-42. doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.332
sources.note: Nothing. Sections: 2 consonants, 3 phonemic vowels/length, 4 syllable, 5 tonal melodies (p. 22ff.), 6 conclusions. Section 5 opens 'Northern Mao, like other Omotic languages, exhibits contrastive tone' and establishes three tone levels with F0 measurements; no mention of stress, accent or prominence in the whole article (a full-text search for stress/accent PDF text and HTML text: zero hits).
